name: Calendar
purpose: The standalone month grid: a whole month, in page flow, sized by its container. Weekday heads, whole week rows (out-of-month days drawn, not hidden), full keyboard grid navigation, month and year paging, ink-knockout selection, a structural today ring and a disabled treatment for out-of-range days. Built #210 wave 4 (heavy seven). PROPOSED, NOT RULED — nothing is registered and every question in the receipt is Dave's.

props.name: month
props.$note: The month in view. Week starts Monday (en-GB), as Date-picker does.

props.name: value
props.$note: The selected day, or nothing. Single selection only — range selection is NOT drawn and is not this component's claim (see Date-range picker, and receipt Q5).

props.name: minDate/maxDate
props.$note: Days outside the range render disabled (text/disabled, the Date-picker treatment, in lock-step). The live specimen disables everything before today so the treatment is visible — a demo choice, not a rule.

props.name: showAdjacentMonths
props.$note: PROPOSED default. True draws the leading and trailing days of the neighbouring months at a readable recessive ink so week rows are whole; false would leave holes in the grid the way Date-picker's panel does. Receipt Q3 asks Dave which is the house default and whether those days should be selectable.

variants.name: standalone
variants.use: The month living in page flow — a journey step, a booking screen, a statement-period chooser. This is the component.

variants.name: narrow
variants.use: The same markup in a ~288px seat: columns are 1fr and cells keep their 40px minimum height, so it narrows with no breakpoint of its own.

$states: today and selected (ring flips to background/default)
$consumes: Date-picker (day-cell state language and keyboard model — lock-step; change it there)

dimensions.width: NONE — width is the container's (#210 discipline). Columns are 1fr; no max-width is declared on .cal.

tokens.surface: background/default on a 1px border/subtle box, border-radius/surface
tokens.selection: ink knockout — text/default fill + background/default numeral (the tooltip precedent, via Date-picker)
tokens.today: 2px inset ring on form/border/active — a SHAPE, never colour alone; aria-current carries it too
tokens.todayAndSelected: the ring flips to background/default so it survives inside the knockout (see antiPatterns)
tokens.outOfMonth: text/default at --alpha-60 — a READABLE recessive ink, deliberately NOT text/disabled
tokens.focus: focus/ring, 2px, inset by -2px so it survives the 4px cell gap
tokens.motion: component-type/button-family/press-travel + press-darken on .cal-nav — AUTO-PARTIAL markers in place, injection pending conductor registration

behaviour.keyboard: One tab stop (roving tabindex). Arrows move by day and week and page the view at a month edge; Home and End go to the week's edges; PageUp and PageDown change month, with Shift they change year; Enter and Space select. Identical to Date-picker's model, deliberately.
behaviour.select: Sets aria-selected on the day and announces it through a polite live region. There is no field to write into and nothing to dismiss — that is the whole difference from Date-picker.
behaviour.outOfMonthDays: Drawn and announced, NOT focusable and NOT selectable — they are spans, not buttons. Crossing a month edge with an arrow key pages the view instead. PROPOSED; receipt Q3.
behaviour.disabledDays: Rendered as disabled buttons; the roving stop is kept off them.

accessibility.structure: A real <table> with role=grid and a visually-hidden <caption> carrying the month. Rows are <tr role=row>, weekday heads are <th role=columnheader scope=col abbr=...>, and cells are plain <td> whose role maps NATIVELY to gridcell because the table's role is grid (HTML-AAM). The redundant role attributes were removed rather than written — first rule of ARIA — and the computed roles were then verified in a real browser rather than asserted.
accessibility.states: aria-selected on every day button; aria-current=date on today (the ring is never the only channel); disabled days carry the native disabled attribute and an 'Unavailable, ...' accessible name.
accessibility.names: Every day carries a full date accessible name ('16 September 2026'), so a screen reader never has to reconstruct the month from a bare numeral.
accessibility.focus: 2px focus/ring inset by -2px; input-modality data attribute is set so pointer users do not see keyboard rings.
accessibility.live: The month title is aria-live=polite, so paging announces the new month.
accessibility.$gate-note: The a11y gate's role vocabulary in _a11y_target.py contains neither `gridcell` nor `rowgroup`. This component surfaced that gap (a first draft wrote both roles explicitly and the gate failed loud); the gap is REAL and is declared in the #210 lane-A receipt for the conductor. Date-picker never surfaced it because its grid is built in JavaScript and no static gate can see JavaScript-built markup.

antiPatterns: Hiding out-of-month days in a month that is READ — a week row with a hole in it is not a week (Date-picker's panel is a different case: it is a transient act of picking).
Dimming out-of-month days to text/disabled. They are not disabled, they are adjacent, and the disabled ink measures 1.42:1 on white — the #209 cancelled-mandate class.
Leaving the today ring on form/border/active when the day is also selected: it then paints near-black on the near-black knockout and measures 1.06:1. The ring must flip to background/default.
Colour-alone marking of today or selected (today = ring + aria-current; selected = knockout + aria-selected).
Baking a fixed width or max-width into the component. Width is the container's.
Local press-physics CSS on .cal-nav (ADR-0013: physics arrives via the injected partial).
Press physics on day cells — a day is a selection target, not a button (Date-picker's choice, followed in lock-step).
A second tab stop inside the grid. One roving stop, always.

responsive.rule: Columns are 1fr in a table-layout:fixed grid; cells hold a 40px minimum height. No component-level breakpoint exists — only the demo page has one, at 480px, for its own chrome.
responsive.verified: Driven in headless Chromium at 1180px and at a 288px container; figures in the #210 lane-A receipt.

tokenValidation.against: current store (the light and dark values are the same ones Date-picker and Accordion declare)
tokenValidation.result: PASS — no new token minted, no colour invented. Day-cell chrome = Date-picker's live form/* and text/* set; the surface rule = border/subtle; nav geometry and motion params = component-type/button-family, byte-identical to Date-picker's.
tokenValidation.$note: Out-of-month days and weekday heads paint text/default at --alpha-60, a COMPOSED value that no abstract token pair can describe. They are measured in a real browser and the figures live in the receipt, rather than asserted as a contrastPair.

provenance.$note: #210 wave 4, lane A, from the heavy-seven fan-out brief (notes/_briefs/2026-08-20-210-wave4-heavy7-fanout-brief-v1.md). Premise re-probed in-lane: `ls knowledge/snippets/ | grep -icE '^Calendar\.'` returned 0. Authority for the day-cell language and the keyboard model is the gated Date-picker snippet; the surface is the card idiom. No Figma node bound. PROPOSED, never promoted — no registration of any kind was taken by this lane.

$relationship-to-date-picker: PROPOSED, NOT ADJUDICATED (the brief fences this explicitly). Date-picker is a FIELD that owns a calendar: an Input-fields boxed input plus an anchored dismissable panel whose job is to write DD/MM/YYYY back. Calendar is the month grid on its own. The proposal is that Date-picker's panel should CONSUME this organism rather than keep a second copy of the grid; it does not today, and this lane did not edit Date-picker because it is gated and promoted. Whether they merge, whether Calendar is deleted, or whether both stand is DAVE'S — receipt Q1.
